critic_summary: Targeted failure mode: the previous method's falsification step calibrates on one or two hand-picked train dates, with no check that the candidate's binding feature has the same distribution on the other dates. Loop 5's wide-spread gate was calibrated on dense-trade dates (~6% wide-spread arrivals on 20260316/20260318) but on early-window thin-trade dates wide spreads were >99% of arrivals — the gate effectively skipped everything there, forgoing ~$871 of parent edge across 20260308-20260311. The win was real but partly coincidental: it came from a dense-day loss tail the test happened to identify, not from a mechanism the calibration showed to be regime-robust. The new method inserts (a) a Step 3 binding-feature regime audit across every train date (cheap pandas per-date, on parent CSVs already on disk), with a HOMOGENEOUS/HETEROGENEOUS verdict stated before falsification; (b) a Step 4 protocol switch — HETEROGENEOUS candidates require per-date sign-consistency falsification (e.g., ≥ 8 of 12 dates) using every train date, not a hand-picked subset; (c) a Step 5 regime-coverage prediction (how many train dates should fire ≥ 5% of arrivals — extremes are warning signs); and (d) a Step 6 regime-aware parameter rule that forces thresholds on heterogeneous binding features to be regime-relative (e.g., k × rolling_median_in_session) rather than absolute. Gate result: 4/5 metrics improved vs running-best loop 1 (pnl 1471.75 vs 1062.25, sharpe 13.72 vs 4.19, max_dd -0.0164 vs -0.0427, win-rate 0.3547 vs 0.3539; mean_slippage tied at 0). Caveat: the loop-5 aggregate is over 11/12 train dates because 20260319 OOM'd in the runner (Rust allocator 4 GiB cap, a runner-level issue independent of algorithm logic); even if 20260319 had added $0 to l5, the absolute pnl margin over loop 1 is ~$409 and the gate verdict is robust to that missing date. The win-rate margin is thin (~+0.0008) and could plausibly invert with the missing date — but with 4 of 5 metrics clearly improved, the gate holds. If the new method works, the next reasoning trace will show: a per-train-date table for each candidate's binding feature, an explicit heterogeneity verdict stated before falsification, falsification statistics aggregated across the full train window (not 1-2 dates) for any heterogeneous candidate, a regime-coverage prediction listed in NOTES.md, and either a regime-relative threshold parameterization or an explicit justification that the binding feature was homogeneous enough to permit an absolute threshold.
